summary: This bill designates the USPS facility at 6444 San Fernando Road in Glendale, California, as the Paul Ignatius Post Office and requires all official references to use that name.

scores.thoughts: The bill is a straightforward designation of a postal facility name. It contains no provisions that authorize, increase, decrease, or otherwise modify any government expenditures or appropriations.
No provisions in the bill relate to tax rates, tax policy, revenue collection, or any tax-related matters.
The legislation addresses only the naming of a postal facility and has no connection to healthcare policy, coverage, or regulation.
The bill contains nothing related to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No immigration, border security, or visa provisions appear in the text.
The bill does not address reproductive rights, abortion access, or any related healthcare regulations.
While the honoree (Paul Ignatius) had a prior career in defense, the bill itself is limited to a postal facility naming and does not alter military or defense spending or policy.
No environmental, climate, or regulatory provisions are present.
The legislation does not modify or reference any welfare, entitlement, or social safety-net programs.
No education funding, policy, or school-related content exists in the bill.
The bill has no provisions concerning drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance regulation.
Nothing in the text relates to sentencing, policing, incarceration, or criminal justice reform.
The bill does not address tariffs, trade agreements, or international commerce.
No fiscal measures affecting deficits, debt ceiling, or debt reduction are included.
The legislation contains no provisions regarding LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
No foreign aid, international assistance, or diplomatic funding provisions are present.
The bill does not touch on voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight content exists.
The bill does not address labor rights, union protections, or employment policy.
No provisions relate to religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or anti-discrimination law.
